relationships.description: Commission opened investigation against Company.
Commission fined Company €500 million in Article 5 (4) Investigation.
Commission issued cease and desist order requiring removal of restrictions preventing developers from steering users to alternative distribution channels.
Commission issued preliminary findings in Article 6 (4) Investigation.
Commission may issue cease and desist order and impose fines up to 10% of Company's annual worldwide net sales if violation found.
Commission may seek additional fines if Company violated cease and desist order.
Company appealed Commission's Article 5 (4) decision.
Company believes it complies with DMA.
Company made changes to compliance plan.
DOJ filed civil antitrust lawsuit against Company.

relationships.target: U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey
relationships.description: DOJ filed lawsuit in U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey.
DOJ alleged violations of U.S. antitrust laws.
DOJ seeks equitable relief.
DOJ seeks monetary damages.
DOJ seeks nonmonetary relief.
DOJ has substantial defenses.
Epic Games filed lawsuit against Company.
California District Court found App Review Guidelines violate California's unfair competition law.
California District Court issued 2021 Injunction.
2021 Injunction enjoined Company from prohibiting developers from including certain calls to action.
California District Court enjoined Company from imposing commission or fee on purchases outside an app.
Company appealed California District Court’s April 2025 decision to Ninth Circuit Court.
Ninth Circuit Court upheld 2025 Injunction in part and modified aspects.
Ninth Circuit Court held that Company can charge commission on link‑out purchases.
Ninth Circuit Court remanded to California District Court to further amend or modify 2025 Injunction.
Deadline for Company to file petition for rehearing is March 2, 2026.
